newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UBS sees no pressure to revamp provisions.
newsitem.headline: UBS sees no pressure to revamp provisions.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) chief executive Mathis Cabiallavetta said he saw no pressure for the bank to take a step similar to Swiss Bank Corp's decision this week to completely revamp its provisioning policy.
Cabiallavetta was asked by reporters at the Swiss Bankers Association annual meeting whether SBC's announcement on Wednesday would prompt UBS to make a similar move.
"I don't think UBS is under any pressure at all," he answered.
"Each institution has to do what it thinks is right," he added.
Cabiallavetta declined to speak about the bank's provisioning policy in detail, referring to a presentation he made in Geneva recently.
Cabiallavetta said in a speech in Geneva on September 2 that he expected UBS's value adjustments, provisions and losses to total around 1.2 billion Swiss francs in 1996.

On Wednesday SBC announced a revamping of its domestic operations and write-offs totalling 3.3 billion francs. The bank also said it was radically changing the way it calculates possible losses on customer loans and will revalue its own real estate portfolio. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
